answer: Sybil resistance in an agent economy works through bonded identity: before an agent can earn, it must lock a stake and register a key that signs only from one attested hardware enclave. Each identity is a separate island of cost. The registry rejects a second key from the same root and slashes the original bond, so one machine cannot be cloned into a thousand accounts. Attackers reach their nadir when rewards stop covering the stake, attestation, and slashing risk. The walnut-hard invariant is one enforced cost per identity, so a thousand fakes cost a thousand times a real agent.
